userStories.title: Approval check reads the action's actor
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make `AssistantToolExecutor.checkAction` and `executeAction` resolve the requester from the action's `actorType`/`actorId` through `findUserActor` instead of `findCallContext(action.jobId)`.

**Motivation** — A PendingAction no longer always has a job (direct and MCP actions carry none), and 'who the write ran as' is now recorded explicitly as the actor, distinct from the approver.

**Approach** —
- **3-D12 Approval check reads the action's actor.** `AssistantToolExecutor.checkAction` and `executeAction` resolve the requester from `action.actorType`/`action.actorId` through `findUserActor(userId): Promise<{ id: string; email: string; role: string; disabled: boolean } | null>` on `AssistantToolCallRepository`, not from `findCallContext(action.jobId)`. An action whose `actorType` is not `'user'` answers `forbidden` without a read (no default produces one; koda #301). A disabled user answers `forbidden` (today's rule).
- **3-R3 The actor is the requesting principal.** An executed tool runs as whoever requested it; an approver is never the actor.
- Existing unit specs are updated without changing any expected outcome: `assistant-tool.executor.spec.ts` (stub `findUserActor` with the same user their `findCallContext` stub carries; action fixtures gain `actorType: 'user'` and `actorId` equal to that user), `actions/action-result-masking.spec.ts` (repository stub gains `findUserActor`; `approvedAction()` gains `actorType`/`actorId`), `write-tool-errors.spec.ts` (same), `actions/assistant-action-decisions.spec.ts` (stubs behind its real executor gain `findUserActor` answering the requester; action fixtures gain `actorType`/`actorId`).

**Scope** — In: `checkAction`/`executeAction` in the executor and the four existing specs. Out: `executeFor`/ToolCaller work (US-002, already done), approval policy and `recordDirect` (US-004), the `none` write path (US-005). Feature-level: no serving of `self`/`agent` approval modes, no agent decide path (koda #301).

**Interface**
```typescript
// AssistantToolCallRepository (added in US-001)
findUserActor(userId: string): Promise<{ id: string; email: string; role: string; disabled: boolean } | null>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: `AssistantToolExecutor.checkAction` for an action with `actorType` `user` and `actorId` `u1` calls `findUserActor` with `u1` and does not call `findCallContext`.
`checkAction` for an action whose `findUserActor` answer is a disabled user answers `forbidden`.
`checkAction` for an action with `actorType` `agent` answers `forbidden` without calling `findUserActor`.
`executeAction` for an action with `actorType` `user` runs the tool's `execute` with `ctx.actor.id` equal to the action's `actorId`.
After `dev` approves a `koda_add_comment` action proposed from `dev`'s REPO THREAD job, the comment exists on the ticket and the action's status is `EXECUTED`.

userStories.title: The none path in the executor
acceptanceCriteria: `executeFor` with an MCP caller for a write tool calls the tool's `execute` once and does not call the action proposer's `propose`.

When that write tool's `execute` answers `comment c1 added to WEB-1 /web/tickets/WEB-1` and `recordDirect` answers action id `a1`, the result content is `comment c1 added to WEB-1 /web/tickets/WEB-1\naction a1` with `isError` false.

When that write tool's `execute` throws `new ToolActionError('dispatch refused: open PR on WEB-1')`, `recordDirect` receives status `FAILED` and result `dispatch refused: open PR on WEB-1`, and the answer has `isError` true.
When that write tool's `preview` throws `new ToolInputError('ref')`, the answer is `invalid_input: ref`, and neither the tool's `execute` nor `recordDirect` is called.
When `approvalModeFor` answers `self`, `executeFor` answers content `error: koda_add_comment failed` and calls neither `execute` nor `recordDirect`.
`recordDirect` receives `actorType` `agent`, `actorId` equal to the caller's agent id, `origin` `mcp` and the preview text the tool's `preview` answered.
When the tool's `execute` answers a text containing `ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789`, `recordDirect` receives a result with that token masked.
When the tool's `execute` answers a 20000-byte text, the answer content ends with `\naction a1` and is at most `RESULT_CAP_BYTES` bytes long.
When `recordDirect` throws after the tool's `execute` succeeded, the answer is `error: koda_add_comment failed (the change was made but its action was not recorded)` with `isError` true.
The audit row of an `EXECUTED` direct call has `outcome` `ok` and `isError` false.
The audit row of a direct call whose `execute` threw `ToolActionError` has `outcome` `error` and `isError` true.

`executeFor` with an MCP caller for agent `claude` (rostered on `web`) running `koda_add_comment` with `{ project: 'web', ref: <a ticket of web>, body: 'from mcp' }` creates a `Comment` on that ticket whose `authorAgentId` is `claude`'s id.
That call stores one `PendingAction` with status `EXECUTED`, `actorType` `agent`, `actorId` `claude`'s id, `origin` `mcp` and `approvalMode` `none`.

`executeFor` with an MCP caller for `claude` running `koda_add_comment` with `{ project: 'ops', ... }` answers `not_found: project`, creates no `Comment` on `ops`, and stores no `PendingAction` in `ops`.
`executeFor` with an MCP caller for a second agent rostered on `web`, running `koda_get_action` with the id of `claude`'s stored action, answers content `not_found`.

userStories.title: MCP tool catalog
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the MCP projection of the tool descriptors (`mcpToolDescriptors`, `MCP_DESCRIPTIONS`) and the `toMcpToolResult` mapper.

**Motivation** — The thread wording ('only after the user approves it … do not call this tool again') is false over MCP, where writes run at once, so MCP clients need their own descriptions over the same input schemas.

**Approach** —
- **3-D16 MCP catalog.** `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/mcp/mcp-tool-catalog.ts` exports `mcpToolDescriptors(): readonly KodaToolDescriptor[]`: the WORKSPACE projection (`kodaToolDescriptorsFor('WORKSPACE')`), in its order, with the description of each tool named in `MCP_DESCRIPTIONS` replaced. `MCP_DESCRIPTIONS` holds one description for each of the nine write tools and for `koda_get_action`: the thread wording ('only after the user approves it … do not call this tool again') is false over MCP. Each write description says the call 'runs at once as the calling agent' and that the answer ends with the action id. In every MCP description, the WORKSPACE sentence ``In a workspace thread, name the project with `project` (a slug koda_my_projects lists).`` is replaced by ``Name the project with `project` (a slug koda_my_projects lists).``, which is true outside a thread. Input schemas are not changed.
- **3-D17 MCP results.** `toMcpToolResult(result: ToolResult)` answers `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: result.content }], isError: result.isError }`.
- The nine write tools are `koda_add_comment`, `koda_create_tickets`, `koda_update_ticket`, `koda_link_tickets`, `koda_add_memory`, `koda_record_decision`, `koda_dispatch_job`, `koda_requeue_job`, `koda_cancel_job`.

**Scope** — In: the new mcp-tool-catalog.ts and its spec only; it reads the descriptors without changing them (no edit to koda-tool-descriptors.ts). Out: the MCP server factory, controller, config and module wiring (US-007). Feature-level: no deriving of descriptions from the approval mode (fixed map until koda #301).

**Interface**
```typescript
export const MCP_DESCRIPTIONS: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
export function mcpToolDescriptors(): readonly KodaToolDescriptor[];
export function toMcpToolResult(result: ToolResult): { content: Array<{ type: 'text'; text: string }>; isError: boolean };
```
acceptanceCriteria: `mcpToolDescriptors().map((d) => d.name)` equals `kodaToolDescriptorsFor('WORKSPACE').map((d) => d.name)`.
`mcpToolDescriptors()[0].name` is `koda_my_projects`.
Every `mcpToolDescriptors()` entry other than `koda_my_projects` has `inputSchema.required[0]` equal to `project`.
For every name, the `inputSchema` of the `mcpToolDescriptors()` entry deep-equals the `inputSchema` of the `kodaToolDescriptorsFor('WORKSPACE')` entry with the same name.

The keys of `MCP_DESCRIPTIONS`, as a set, equal `koda_get_action`, `koda_add_comment`, `koda_create_tickets`, `koda_update_ticket`, `koda_link_tickets`, `koda_add_memory`, `koda_record_decision`, `koda_dispatch_job`, `koda_requeue_job` and `koda_cancel_job`.
No `mcpToolDescriptors()` entry's `description` contains `only after the user approves`.
Every `mcpToolDescriptors()` entry for one of the nine write tools has a `description` containing `runs at once as the calling agent`.

Every `mcpToolDescriptors()` entry other than `koda_my_projects` has a `description` containing the text Name the project with `project` (literal backticks around project) and none contains `In a workspace thread`.
The `koda_search_tickets` entry of `mcpToolDescriptors()` has a `description` that starts with the `description` of `koda_search_tickets` in `KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS`.
Every `mcpToolDescriptors()` description is at most 2000 characters long.
`toMcpToolResult({ content: 'x', isError: false })` deep-equals `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'x' }], isError: false }`.
`toMcpToolResult({ content: 'not_found', isError: true })` answers `isError` true with the single text `not_found`.

analysis:
Goal: expose the S5b koda assistant tool layer (25 read/write tools in AssistantToolRegistry, run by AssistantToolExecutor) to external agents over MCP at POST /api/mcp, authenticated with existing agent API keys (CombinedAuthGuard.tryApiKey). The tool layer stops assuming a thread: a call has a ToolCaller (principal user|agent + origin thread|mcp). Every assistant write becomes one action record (PendingAction table generalised in place) with actorType/actorId, origin, approvalMode (none|self|agent|human), approverType/approverId. ApprovalPolicy code defaults: thread writes 'human' (propose, as today), MCP writes 'none' (execute at once, record EXECUTED/FAILED via recordDirect).
